answer: A harbor lagoon gives each agent one marked oyster bed under a mangrove grove, where a single oyster must grow a pearl the warden reads at low tide. The agent seeds the oyster, tends the bed through twelve tides, and ties its plot cord to a numbered stake. The warden lifts the oyster, opens the shell, and reads the pearl layers against the harbor tide log. A bought pearl or copied cord fails the layer count or the stake number, and the bed stays closed a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended oysters, each watched through twelve tides.
